name: RadioIndex (The Archive of American Radio)

pricing.billingNote: 100% open public archival access; zero ads, zero paywalls, zero tracking.
pricing.freeTierNote: Full catalog streaming, synchronized .vtt transcripts, podcast RSS feeds, and JSON APIs included.

provenance.primaryMasterSource: 16" ET lacquer transfers, AFRS pressings, network line checks, and deduplicated OTRR/IA masters with SHA-256 stream digests
provenance.airdateMethodology: Primary newspaper radio logs (Chronicling America, Fulton History, JJonz, Variety, Broadcasting) + full-audio verbal announcement verification; zero stride projection
provenance.castAttributionMethod: Episode-specific faster-whisper VAD full-audio transcription + primary studio script reconciliation linking actors to exact character roles
provenance.captionEngine: 100% full-length faster-whisper (large-v3 + VAD filtering) WebVTT synchronized captions

summary: Research-grade public broadcast archive running on a pure Rust HTML-over-the-wire origin. Enforces strict primary-evidence air date corroboration, full-length faster-whisper WebVTT transcription, per-episode character role mapping, and cryptographic stream deduplication.

primary_source_verification.summary: Every broadcast date is cross-checked against historic newspaper radio logs (Chronicling America, Fulton History, JJonz) or explicit in-recording announcements.
primary_source_verification.evidenceQuote: "NEVER SYNTHESIZE AIR DATES: Never project, extrapolate, or calculate broadcast air dates via calendar stride projection... Every air date must be corroborated by primary archival logs."

cast_credit_accuracy.summary: Per-episode Cast & Crew links[] reconcile spoken sign-off credits and archival logs to exact character roles; never copies series leads blindly.
cast_credit_accuracy.evidenceQuote: "Every cast credit and character assignment must be explicitly verified through full-length speech-to-text audio transcription or primary archival radio logs/scripts."

vtt_transcripts.summary: 100% full-length audio WebVTT (.vtt) transcripts generated with faster-whisper + VAD filtering and synchronized in the Now Playing drawer.
vtt_transcripts.evidenceQuote: "Always pass the entire full-length .vtt transcript from start to finish... synchronized word/phrase cues served via radioindex.org-subtitles."

master_provenance.summary: Tracks SHA-256 stream digests, 16" ET matrix numbers, AFRS numbers, and separates East/West network feeds.
master_provenance.evidenceQuote: "Stream records store cryptographic digests, source transfer lineage, and blocked-stream-digests to purge corrupt or mislabeled encodes."

serial_continuity.summary: Contiguous multi-part story arcs (Johnny Dollar 5-parters, I Love a Mystery, CBSRMT) ordered chronologically with verified broadcast numbers.
serial_continuity.evidenceQuote: "Series listings (/search?series=) and curated shelves preserve chronological broadcast sequence and multi-part serial continuity."

open_api_export.summary: Deterministic query-string routes (/search?series=, /listen?id=, /rss?series=), HTML fragments (/api/fragments), and open Git-backed data repos.
open_api_export.evidenceQuote: "Public URLs are a top-level route plus a query string only (/search?series=, /listen?id=, /rss?series=); data lives in open git repos."

ad_free_playback.summary: Zero commercial interruptions, zero banner ads, and zero paywalls; original 1930s–1950s sponsor announcements preserved intact.
ad_free_playback.evidenceQuote: "Free public access served directly from OVH Rust origin with persistent mini-player and expanded Now Playing queue."

dedup_integrity.summary: Moves duplicate recordings onto the canonical broadcast winner while preserving active East/West coast variant recordings.
dedup_integrity.evidenceQuote: "When two broadcasts are duplicates (same title + date in same program): move all recordings to the winner, set is_active=0 on the loser. Never hard-delete."

gotchas.title: Strict Ground-Truth Gate Delays Unverified Uploads
gotchas.detail: Episodes lacking verifiable primary air dates or awaiting full-length faster-whisper VAD transcription are flagged rather than guessed, meaning newly discovered raw trader tapes take longer to pass enrichment QA.

gotchas.title: Retired Legacy Path URLs Redirect via 301
gotchas.detail: Older path-style URLs (/series/*, /broadcasts/*, /episodes/*) are retired in favor of flat query routes (/search?series=, /listen?id=) with 301 redirects.

specNotes.uuid_index: Canonical UUID & short RID per broadcast/recording (/listen?id={id}, radioindex.org-ids) for universal stream & subtitle resolution.
specNotes.sha256_dedup: Cryptographic SHA-256 stream digests across all mirrors; preserves separate East/West Coast network broadcasts.
specNotes.vtt_subtitles: 231,400+ full-length faster-whisper VAD WebVTT (.vtt) subtitle files synced in-player and downloadable.
specNotes.newspaper_scans: Direct citations to scanned newspaper radio logs (Chronicling America, Fulton History, JJonz, Variety, Broadcasting).
specNotes.studio_scripts: Original studio continuity and production scripts linked via radioindex.org-scripts.
specNotes.schema_jsonld: Full Schema.org RadioEpisode & RadioSeries JSON-LD + OpenGraph on every broadcast route.

name: Internet Archive — OTRR & Old Time Radio Collection

pricing.billingNote: Non-profit public digital library funded by donations and grants.
pricing.freeTierNote: Unlimited HTTP downloads, Torrents, IA S3 CLI access, and in-browser BookReader/Audio playback.

provenance.primaryMasterSource: Crowdsourced uploads ranging from pristine 16" ET FLAC rips to 5th-gen 32 kbps MP3 cassette dubs
provenance.airdateMethodology: Uploader-supplied filenames (YY-MM-DD); mixes OTRR Certified research with unverified trader logs
provenance.castAttributionMethod: Free-text item description box; no structured episode-level cast or character schema
provenance.captionEngine: Scattered OCR/auto-ASR on select items; >92% of OTR audio items lack synchronized .vtt files

summary: The foundational raw storage commons of the OTR ecosystem. Hosts nearly 100,000 audio files including official OTRR Certified series sets and rare 16" ET transfers, but suffers from severe item-level fragmentation, duplicate uploads, slow Web player startup on 500-file items, and inconsistent metadata.

primary_source_verification.summary: OTRR Certified uploads include researcher log PDFs, but thousands of older user uploads rely on unverified 1990s trader filenames.
primary_source_verification.evidenceQuote: "Metadata is user-contributed per item; single episodes frequently appear across 6+ items with conflicting YY-MM-DD filename prefixes."

cast_credit_accuracy.summary: Item-level XML (`_meta.xml`) applies to whole 200-episode ZIP buckets rather than individual episodes or character roles.
cast_credit_accuracy.evidenceQuote: "Creator and description tags live at the collection/item container level, not per MP3 track inside a multi-file upload."

vtt_transcripts.summary: No systematic WebVTT caption corpus across OTR collections; web player streams raw MP3/Ogg without synchronized dialogue text.
vtt_transcripts.evidenceQuote: "Audio items contain derivative .mp3 and .ogg files plus waveform .pngs, with no synchronized .vtt track derivatives."

master_provenance.summary: Hosts some extraordinary direct 16" transcription disc transfers (e.g., AFRS, NBC, Goldin/Marr donations) alongside undocumented 32k re-encodes.
master_provenance.evidenceQuote: "Includes lossless 16-bit/44.1kHz and 24-bit/96kHz FLAC transfers when uploaded by preservationists, mixed with legacy 32 kbps MP3s."

serial_continuity.summary: Works when filenames strictly obey `YYMMDD_Ep#` sorting inside a single item, but breaks when episodes span multiple uploader items.
serial_continuity.evidenceQuote: "Track order in the JWPlayer playlist depends entirely on ASCII sorting of filenames in `_files.xml`."

open_api_export.summary: Full `ia` CLI, Advanced Search JSON API, S3-like bucket URLs (`/download/<item>/`), and torrent manifests.
open_api_export.evidenceQuote: "Internet Archive Metadata API (`/metadata/{identifier}`) exposes full file lists, SHA1/MD5 hashes, and direct HTTP download links."

ad_free_playback.summary: 100% free and ad-free, though high-file-count items experience slow playlist DOM initialization.
ad_free_playback.evidenceQuote: "No commercial ads or paywalls; occasional rate-limiting or maintenance downtime during peak archive crawls."

dedup_integrity.summary: Zero cross-item deduplication; the same *Suspense* or *Shadow* recording is routinely duplicated 8 to 15 times across different uploader buckets.
dedup_integrity.evidenceQuote: "Each uploader creates an independent item identifier (`OTRR_Suspense_Singles`, `suspense-otr`, `Suspense_1942-1962`), resulting in massive duplication."

gotchas.title: Container-Level Metadata Granularity Trap
gotchas.detail: Because an Internet Archive 'Item' often holds 100 to 600 MP3 files, item-level metadata (`_meta.xml`) cannot express per-episode air dates, cast lists, or synopses.

gotchas.title: High-Latency Playlist Boot on Large Items
gotchas.detail: Opening an IA item page with 500+ MP3s + derivatives forces the browser to parse megabytes of playlist JSON before first audio frame playback.

gotchas.title: Derivative Re-Encoding Artifacts
gotchas.detail: IA's automated derivative pipeline historically generated 64k VBR MP3 and Ogg derivatives from already-lossy 32k–64k MP3 uploads, compounding generational artifacts if users stream the derivative instead of the original.

specNotes.uuid_index: Uses uploader-chosen folder slugs (/details/{slug}) with 50–500 MP3s bundled into one item; no per-broadcast canonical UUID.
specNotes.sha256_dedup: File-level MD5/SHA1 per upload bucket, but identical broadcasts are duplicated across dozens of overlapping uploader items.
specNotes.vtt_subtitles: Over 95% of OTR audio files have no .vtt caption track.
specNotes.schema_jsonld: No Schema.org RadioEpisode JSON-LD markup on item pages.

name: RUSC (Radio U S C)

pricing.billingNote: Recurring commercial subscription required for full streaming and MP3 downloads ($4.99/mo billed annually).
pricing.freeTierNote: Small rotating sample of free introductory shows; full 35,000+ catalog is behind a subscriber login wall.

provenance.primaryMasterSource: Legacy collector sets & OTRR public-domain transfers normalized to compact 32–64 kbps mono MP3
provenance.airdateMethodology: Collector log dates imported from legacy OTR databases without primary newspaper citations
provenance.castAttributionMethod: Series-level star tags and editorial blurbs; rare supporting actors omitted

summary: Long-running commercial OTR membership site with warm community curation, themed playlists (Christmas, Detective, Sci-Fi), and editorial synopses. However, it paywalls public-domain recordings, compresses audio to low bitrates (32–64 kbps), and lacks transcripts or primary archival citations.

primary_source_verification.summary: Air dates are inherited from 1990s/2000s collector logs without newspaper radio log citations or corrections for stride-projected soaps.
primary_source_verification.evidenceQuote: "Displays a single date string per show entry with no citation to newspaper logs, network ledgers, or disc matrix numbers."

cast_credit_accuracy.summary: Links shows to headline stars (e.g., Orson Welles, Vincent Price, Bob Bailey) but lacks verified episode-level character-to-actor mappings.
cast_credit_accuracy.evidenceQuote: "Search by Star groups episodes by main series lead or notable guest star rather than full per-episode cast & character rosters."

vtt_transcripts.summary: Zero WebVTT captions or full-text transcripts.
vtt_transcripts.evidenceQuote: "Provides a short 1–3 sentence editorial description per episode; no spoken dialogue transcription."

master_provenance.summary: Files are standardized at low bitrates (typically 32–56 kbps mono MP3) originally chosen for dial-up/early broadband downloads, with no source lineage.
master_provenance.evidenceQuote: "Audio files are optimized for small file size (5–12 MB per 30-minute show) with no transfer source or disc provenance metadata."

serial_continuity.summary: Editorial playlists group some serial runs together, and chronological series tables help listeners follow multi-part stories.
serial_continuity.evidenceQuote: "Curated playlists and series pages list episodes by episode number and date for sequential listening."

open_api_export.summary: Proprietary authenticated session wall; no public JSON API, no `/llms.txt`, and no bulk export.
open_api_export.evidenceQuote: "Requires active member authentication cookie for MP3 download/stream links; no public developer API."

ad_free_playback.summary: Ad-free inside the player, but requires a $7.95/mo ($59.95/yr) paid subscription to access public-domain broadcasts.
ad_free_playback.evidenceQuote: "Unlimited access to listen to or download over 35,000 old time radio shows requires a paid RUSC membership."

dedup_integrity.summary: Manual editorial curation removes obvious broken duplicates within a series, though legacy date/title aliases remain.
dedup_integrity.evidenceQuote: "Catalog is manually maintained as a single list per series without cryptographic digest tracking."

gotchas.title: Paywall Over Public-Domain Collector Transfers
gotchas.detail: Charges $7.95/mo ($59.95/yr) for recordings that largely originate from volunteer public-domain OTRR and collector preservation efforts available free on RadioIndex and Internet Archive.

gotchas.title: Dial-Up Era Audio Bitrate Ceiling (32–64 kbps)
gotchas.detail: Many files remain encoded at legacy 32–56 kbps mono MP3 with steep 4.5 kHz low-pass filtering, discarding high-frequency lacquer fidelity.

gotchas.title: Zero Programmatic or Agent Access
gotchas.detail: Closed behind member session cookies with no public RSS feeds per series, no JSON endpoints, and no transcripts.

specNotes.free_no_paywall: Requires paid subscription ($6.95/mo or $59.95/yr) to stream or download full catalog.
specNotes.lossless_et: Files are uniformly down-sampled to 32–56 kbps mono MP3 (22.05 kHz); no FLAC or high-bitrate 16" ET masters.

name: Stupid Potato Old Time Radio

pricing.billingNote: Free web access supported by display ads and affiliate links.
pricing.freeTierNote: Instant browser playback of listed series; no account required.

provenance.primaryMasterSource: Unattributed mirror of early-2000s MP3 trading discs and IA hotlinks
provenance.airdateMethodology: Parsed directly from raw MP3 filenames without verification
provenance.castAttributionMethod: None (Series blurb only)

summary: Casual hobbyist web directory offering quick click-to-play access to popular detective, horror, and comedy OTR shows. Convenient for casual sampling, but relies entirely on unverified filename metadata, low-bitrate MP3s, zero cast credits, and zero transcripts.

primary_source_verification.summary: Dates are scraped directly from legacy MP3 filenames with zero newspaper log or recording verification.
primary_source_verification.evidenceQuote: "Episode lists render raw YY-MM-DD filename tokens directly as broadcast dates, propagating every legacy trader error."

cast_credit_accuracy.summary: No per-episode cast, writer, announcer, or character role data.
cast_credit_accuracy.evidenceQuote: "Only static series-level overview text is provided; individual episode rows show title and filename date only."

vtt_transcripts.summary: No captions, transcripts, or searchable spoken text.
vtt_transcripts.evidenceQuote: "Audio-only HTML5 `<audio>` tag embeds with zero text track elements."

master_provenance.summary: Low-bitrate 24–64 kbps MP3s with stripped ID3 provenance and occasional dead mirror links.
master_provenance.evidenceQuote: "Streams unattributed low-bitrate MP3 encodes inherited from early 2000s CD-ROM trading sets."

serial_continuity.summary: Missing episodes and inconsistent naming frequently break multi-part serial story arcs.
serial_continuity.evidenceQuote: "Multi-part serials suffer from missing intermediate chapters and inconsistent filename numbering."

open_api_export.summary: Static HTML pages only; no JSON API, no `/llms.txt`, and no structured RSS feeds.
open_api_export.evidenceQuote: "Legacy HTML directory structure with no machine-readable API or schema.org Dataset markup."

ad_free_playback.summary: No subscription paywall, but pages carry display advertising and occasional broken external audio embeds.
ad_free_playback.evidenceQuote: "Free browser streaming supported by page banner ads."

dedup_integrity.summary: Duplicate episodes with variant trader titles appear as separate broadcasts.
dedup_integrity.evidenceQuote: "No audio fingerprinting or canonical broadcast reconciliation."

gotchas.title: Zero Metadata Beyond Raw Filename Strings
gotchas.detail: Provides no episode synopses, no cast/character credits, no sponsor logs, and no source provenance — just a bare list of MP3 links.

gotchas.title: 6% Link Rot & Unbuffered External Mirrors
gotchas.detail: Several older series pages hotlink to moved or throttled third-party storage buckets, resulting in stalled audio players.

specNotes.lossless_et: Serves 24–32 kbps legacy MP3 transcodes only.
specNotes.vtt_subtitles: Zero .vtt subtitles, zero cast credits, and zero newspaper log citations.
specNotes.uuid_index: Static HTML links to raw MP3 filenames; no recording UUIDs or API.

name: Old Radio World

pricing.billingNote: Free web streaming with AdSense display units.
pricing.freeTierNote: Direct browser streaming and single-file MP3 downloads.

provenance.primaryMasterSource: Legacy collector MP3 sets (mostly 32–48 kbps mono)
provenance.airdateMethodology: Uncorroborated collector filename dates
provenance.castAttributionMethod: None (Series-level intro paragraph only)

summary: Minimalist, fast-loading web directory covering ~195 popular OTR series. While easy for a casual visitor to click and play a classic *Jack Benny* or *Dimension X* episode, its catalog is a static snapshot of early-2000s low-bitrate MP3s with zero archival verification or transcripts.

primary_source_verification.summary: Uses unverified dates from legacy collector MP3 filenames.
primary_source_verification.evidenceQuote: "Dates are displayed as static strings (`YYYY-MM-DD`) without archival log verification."

cast_credit_accuracy.summary: Lists lead actor in the series summary paragraph only; zero episode-level cast or role data.
cast_credit_accuracy.evidenceQuote: "Individual episode entries contain only Title, Date, and Play/Download links."

vtt_transcripts.summary: No transcripts or captions.
vtt_transcripts.evidenceQuote: "No text transcripts or closed captions provided."

master_provenance.summary: Predominantly 32 kbps and 48 kbps mono MP3s from legacy CD-R trading pools.
master_provenance.evidenceQuote: "Audio files average 4–7 MB per 30-minute broadcast (32 kbps MP3) with no provenance tags."

serial_continuity.summary: Paginated episode tables list shows chronologically when dates are present, but omit missing-episode warnings in serials.
serial_continuity.evidenceQuote: "Paginated tables of 50 episodes per page without serial arc grouping."

open_api_export.summary: No JSON API, no RSS podcast feeds per series, and no bulk export.
open_api_export.evidenceQuote: "Server-rendered HTML tables only; no REST API or RSS feed auto-discovery."

ad_free_playback.summary: Free audio playback without mid-roll audio ads, supported by web page display banners.
ad_free_playback.evidenceQuote: "Free streaming with Google display ad banners surrounding the episode table."

dedup_integrity.summary: Contains duplicate encodes under variant titles common to pre-certified OTRR sets.

gotchas.title: Frozen Pre-Certification Audio Sets
gotchas.detail: Most series have not been updated with newer high-bitrate 16" ET transfers discovered by the archival community over the past 15 years.

gotchas.title: No Searchable Episode Synopses or Credits
gotchas.detail: Users cannot search by guest actor, writer, sponsor, or plot keyword — only by series title and episode title.

specNotes.ad_free: Serves third-party display ads alongside 32 kbps MP3 links.
specNotes.vtt_subtitles: Zero .vtt subtitles or episode-level cast verification.

name: SiriusXM RadioClassics (Channel 148)
operator: SiriusXM Satellite Radio (Curated by Greg Bell)

pricing.billingNote: Requires SiriusXM Streaming or All Access satellite/app subscription.
pricing.freeTierNote: None (Occasional promotional trial periods require credit card).

provenance.primaryMasterSource: Restored broadcast transcription discs and curated collector masters with professional EQ/noise restoration
provenance.airdateMethodology: Host Greg Bell verifies air dates and cast biographies against published radio histories for featured broadcasts
provenance.castAttributionMethod: Spoken host introductions detail lead and supporting character actors (not exposed as structured text/JSON)
provenance.captionEngine: None (Live radio stream + uncaptioned on-demand blocks)

summary: Curated 24/7 linear satellite/app radio channel hosted by OTR historian Greg Bell, paired with rotating 2-hour on-demand themed blocks in the SiriusXM app. Offers superb verbal historical context and clean audio restoration, but provides no searchable archive, no permanent on-demand episode library, and DRM-locked streams.

primary_source_verification.summary: Host Greg Bell provides accurate, researched broadcast dates and production history in spoken intros for every aired show.
primary_source_verification.evidenceQuote: "Greg Bell's spoken introductions cite original network air dates, wartime context, and supporting players."

cast_credit_accuracy.summary: Supporting cast and character names are announced verbally by the host, but are not searchable in a structured web database.
cast_credit_accuracy.evidenceQuote: "Rich verbal cast attribution in audio intros, but app metadata displays only a short block title."

vtt_transcripts.summary: Zero WebVTT transcripts or closed captions on satellite or app streams.
vtt_transcripts.evidenceQuote: "Audio-only DRM stream with no synchronized transcript track."

master_provenance.summary: Uses carefully selected, professionally restored transfers with balanced dynamic range and hum removal.
master_provenance.evidenceQuote: "Broadcast-grade restoration sourced from premier transcription disc collections."

serial_continuity.summary: Occasionally airs 5-part *Johnny Dollar* marathons in a 2-hour block, but listeners cannot browse full series runs on demand.
serial_continuity.evidenceQuote: "Rotating schedule of 2-hour blocks; episodes expire from the app after a few weeks."

open_api_export.summary: Completely closed DRM ecosystem; no direct episode URLs, no RSS, no downloads, and no API.
open_api_export.evidenceQuote: "Encrypted HLS streams restricted to proprietary SiriusXM web/mobile/car receivers."

ad_free_playback.summary: No third-party commercial breaks interrupting stories, but requires a $9.99–$23.99/mo subscription ($120+/yr).
ad_free_playback.evidenceQuote: "Commercial-free channel included in SiriusXM paid subscription tiers."

dedup_integrity.summary: Hand-curated broadcast rotation guarantees zero corrupt or mislabeled duplicate files.
dedup_integrity.evidenceQuote: "Every broadcast is hand-screened and scheduled by channel producer Greg Bell."

gotchas.title: Not an On-Demand Archive (~420 Rotating Shows vs. 100,000+)
gotchas.detail: You cannot look up and play a specific episode of *Suspense* or *Escape* on demand; you can only listen to the live linear stream or ~20 rotating 2-hour on-demand blocks.

gotchas.title: Highest Annual Cost ($120–$280/yr) + DRM Lock-In
gotchas.detail: Requires an ongoing SiriusXM subscription with notorious cancellation friction and zero offline file ownership.

specNotes.free_no_paywall: Requires $10.99–$23.99/mo SiriusXM subscription; linear Channel 148 + rotating on-demand buffer (~2,800 episodes).
specNotes.open_json_api: Closed DRM app stream; no public URLs, no RSS, and no permanent archive.

name: OTRRlib.org (Old Time Radio Researchers Library)
operator: Old Time Radio Researchers Group (Volunteer Non-Profit)

pricing.billingNote: 100% volunteer-run, donation-supported archival file server.
pricing.freeTierNote: Unrestricted direct HTTP MP3 downloads and reference magazine PDFs.

provenance.primaryMasterSource: Community-pooled transcription disc transfers, reel-to-reel upgrades, and OTRR Certified series sets
provenance.airdateMethodology: Volunteer researcher logs cross-checked against trade publications for Certified sets; legacy sets retain collector dates
provenance.castAttributionMethod: Companion HTML/PDF series logs list cast for select series, not embedded in a queryable web API

summary: The direct HTTP distribution server of the Old Time Radio Researchers (OTRR) group. Famous for its 'Certified' series projects where volunteers audit missing episodes and upgrade sound quality, though its bare-bones 1990s HTML directory interface lacks modern search, synchronized transcripts, and relational cast APIs.

primary_source_verification.summary: OTRR Certified sets undergo rigorous volunteer log auditing, though uncertified series folders still carry legacy collector dates.
primary_source_verification.evidenceQuote: "Certified Series sets include an Introduction & Log PDF documenting known broadcast dates and missing episodes."

cast_credit_accuracy.summary: Detailed cast lists exist in separate companion PDF/Excel logs on `otrr.org`, but are not linked to audio playback on `otrrlib.org`.
cast_credit_accuracy.evidenceQuote: "Audio files on otrrlib.org are served via flat directory tables without inline cast/character records."

vtt_transcripts.summary: No synchronized WebVTT transcripts; a small number of scanned PDF scripts exist in the separate reference library.
vtt_transcripts.evidenceQuote: "No `.vtt` or `.srt` timed text tracks accompany the MP3 distribution folders."

master_provenance.summary: Actively replaces muddy encodes with higher-generation transcription disc rips when donated by members.
master_provenance.evidenceQuote: "Upgrade alerts track higher-bitrate replacements from 16-inch transcription discs and reel-to-reel tapes."

serial_continuity.summary: Strict `Series_YY-MM-DD_Ep#_Title.mp3` naming convention keeps multi-part serials in accurate sequential order.
serial_continuity.evidenceQuote: "Standardized OTRR file-naming specification guarantees chronological and episode-number ordering."

open_api_export.summary: Predictable direct HTTP directory paths allow `wget`/`curl` mirroring, but no JSON API, RSS feeds, or `/llms.txt`.
open_api_export.evidenceQuote: "Open HTTP file paths (`/ia2/...`) suitable for batch downloaders, without a structured JSON query API."

ad_free_playback.summary: 100% free and ad-free community service.
ad_free_playback.evidenceQuote: "Maintained by volunteer donations with zero commercial advertising."

dedup_integrity.summary: OTRR verification teams actively hunt down 'aka' title aliases and wrongly dated duplicates within each certified series.
dedup_integrity.evidenceQuote: "Series coordinators audit 'AKA' titles and purge mislabeled episodes from certified releases."

gotchas.title: Legacy Frame/Table UI With Zero Full-Text Search
gotchas.detail: Navigating requires clicking alphabetically through nested HTML tables; there is no unified search bar for episode plots, actors, or dialogue.

gotchas.title: Split Between Audio Server (`otrrlib.org`) and Metadata (`otrr.org`)
gotchas.detail: Historical magazines, scripts, and research logs live on separate sub-sites rather than being unified on a single broadcast resource page.

specNotes.uuid_index: Files are addressed by mutable filename strings (e.g. SERIES_YY-MM-DD_ep_title.mp3) rather than permanent recording UUIDs.
specNotes.schema_jsonld: Legacy static HTML directory tables with zero Schema.org JSON-LD or OpenGraph tags.

name: Library of Congress — Recorded Sound Research Center
operator: U.S. Library of Congress (Packard Campus / NAVCC)

pricing.billingNote: Federal public institution; online digital collections are free, but 90% of holdings require on-site Madison Building listening.
pricing.freeTierNote: ~14,000 digitized radio/recorded sound items streamable online; 150,000+ physical discs require Washington D.C. appointment.

provenance.primaryMasterSource: Original NBC Radio Collection 16" lacquer discs, AFRS master library, CBS/WOR/MBS archival deposits
provenance.airdateMethodology: Primary network master control cards, copyright deposits, and Chronicling America newspaper archive
provenance.castAttributionMethod: MARC/MODS catalog records transcribed from NBC master index cards and disc labels
provenance.captionEngine: Select items only (American Archive of Public Broadcasting integration)

summary: The ultimate physical vault of American broadcast history at the Packard Campus (Culpeper, VA), holding the original NBC Radio Collection, AFRS masters, and CBS deposits. Unrivaled primary provenance, but only ~9% of its radio holdings are streamable online without visiting the Recorded Sound Research Center in person.

primary_source_verification.summary: Gold-standard primary network master cards, studio control logs, and the Chronicling America historic newspaper database.
primary_source_verification.evidenceQuote: "Cataloged directly from NBC master index cards, physical 16-inch lacquer labels, and copyright deposit ledgers."

cast_credit_accuracy.summary: MARC catalog records list principal performers and speakers from studio cards, though dramatic character names are often omitted.
cast_credit_accuracy.evidenceQuote: "MARC 511 (Participant or Performer Note) records principal cast and speakers documented on studio index cards."

vtt_transcripts.summary: Most digitized radio broadcasts lack synchronized WebVTT captions, outside of special exhibits.
vtt_transcripts.evidenceQuote: "Online audio items stream via the LOC media player without universal WebVTT caption tracks."

master_provenance.summary: First-generation physical 16" 33⅓ RPM glass/aluminum-base lacquer discs and network master reels preserved in climate-controlled vaults.
master_provenance.evidenceQuote: "Preserves the original NBC Collection of over 150,000 16-inch lacquer transcription discs at the Packard Campus."

serial_continuity.summary: SONIC catalog orders holdings chronologically by shelf/matrix number, but online availability is fragmentary.
serial_continuity.evidenceQuote: "Searchable via the SONIC (Sound Online Inventory and Catalog) database by date and call number."

open_api_export.summary: Every `loc.gov` item and search supports `?fo=json` REST responses and IIIF/MODS metadata.
open_api_export.evidenceQuote: "The loc.gov JSON API (`?fo=json`) provides programmatic access to catalog records and digital asset URLs."

ad_free_playback.summary: 100% ad-free and free of charge, but >90% of broadcasts are blocked from remote internet streaming due to rights restrictions.
ad_free_playback.evidenceQuote: "Due to copyright and donor restrictions, most NBC and AFRS recordings may only be listened to on-site in the Recorded Sound Research Center."

dedup_integrity.summary: Each physical disc pressing, safety reel, and East/West feed has a distinct shelfmark and matrix number.
dedup_integrity.evidenceQuote: "Library of Congress call numbers and matrix identifiers uniquely distinguish every physical lacquer side."

gotchas.title: 91% of Radio Holdings Require In-Person D.C. Reading Room Visit
gotchas.detail: Because pre-1972 sound recordings and underlying dramatic scripts have complex rights layers, the vast majority of the NBC and AFRS collections cannot be streamed from home.

gotchas.title: SONIC Catalog vs. Digital Audio Split
gotchas.detail: Finding a record in the SONIC inventory (`sonic.loc.gov`) usually returns a physical shelf number (`RWA / LWO`) rather than a playable audio stream.
